newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit weakens on speculation, dollar recovery.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit weakens on speculation, dollar recovery.

text.p: The ringgit weakened further against the dollar in Asian trading on speculative buying of dollar/ringgit and the U.S. unit's recovery against the majors.

They said the dollar buying was triggered by reports that a U.S.-Malaysia consortium had to pay over $1 billion for a stake in South Africa's state telecommunications firm Telkom by next week. Telekom Malaysia and U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc are buying a 30 percent stake in Telkom.
"It's a good excuse to buy dollar/ringgit," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "I didn't see much corporate buying today, it's mostly speculative."
Dealers said there was also some followthrough covering of short dollar positions.
The ringgit's fall also reflected a rebound in the dollar against the major currencies, they said.
"Dollar/ringgit is also moving in line with the dollar/majors," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5152/62 a dollar against 2.5085/95 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
Dealers said players were cautious around 2.5150/60 as this was the level at which Bank Negara Malaysia last intervened.
